Who bills property tax in Delaware

Property tax here is billed locally by county tax offices, and the rate you pay depends mostly on your school district. In Kent County, the tax is the taxable value multiplied by the rate, with the school district setting most of that rate and the county government and county library adding to it.

Two houses of equal value can get different bills, even inside one county. A home in the Colonial school district in New Castle County is billed on different rates than one in Appoquinimink. Read the bill for your own parcel and the district printed on it, not a neighbor's number.

With only three counties, the structure is easy to hold in your head.

  • New Castle County: the northern county, with five school districts that lie entirely within it plus a vocational-technical district.
  • Kent County: the middle county, billed by the Kent County Receiver of Taxes.
  • Sussex County: the southern county, billed through the Sussex County Treasury and Billing offices in Georgetown.

The recent countywide reassessment

A court ordered Delaware to reassess after decades without new values. New Castle and Kent counties had not reassessed since the 1980s and Sussex had not done so since 1974, and a 2020 Court of Chancery ruling followed a 2018 lawsuit over the old system.

House Bill 62 now requires each county to reassess every five years. Kent County's current values are as of July 1, 2023, and New Castle County's are as of July 1, 2024.

The reassessment matters to a seller in two ways. Your assessed value now tracks market value much more closely, so a buyer reading your bill sees a number tied to a recent date. And exemptions and abatements were not built into the new assessed values. They are applied once a rate is set. Roughly a third of owners saw lower taxes, a third higher and a third about the same. A sale does not trigger a reassessment in Kent County.

Due dates and penalties

In Kent and Sussex counties the annual bill is due September 30. New Castle County's tax code sets a July 1 due date with a penalty that starts after September 1, so New Castle owners should check their own bill for the exact deadline.

CountyTax yearBills mailedDueLate cost
KentJune 1 to May 31Typically by mid-August, after school districts set ratesSeptember 30Call the Kent tax office
SussexJuly 1 to June 30Early AugustSeptember 30 (supplemental bills Dec. 31, Mar. 31, June 30)1.5% per month
New CastleSet by 9 Del. C. ch. 86Statement within 30 days after the due dateJuly 1 under 9 Del. C. 86016% after September 1, then 1% each month

A missing bill does not cancel a penalty. Sussex County's tax office says the owner must pay on time even if the bill never arrived, and New Castle's code says the same: not receiving a statement does not excuse timely payment.

New Castle's code also requires the Office of Finance to send at least one written demand for unpaid taxes by December 15 each year. A residential owner with a primary residence and a bill at least $300 above the prior year can qualify for a payment plan of at least three equal school-tax installments.

School tax rates

New Castle County has five districts that lie entirely within the county plus a vocational-technical district, and each sets its own rate. Recently the districts split their rates so that homes are charged a lower rate than apartments, commercial and industrial property. Overpayments of more than $50 can be refunded or credited when bills are recalculated.

To estimate a school bill, divide the assessment by 100 and multiply by the residential rate for your district. Rates are set after school boards vote each summer and change from year to year, so use the rate printed on your current bill instead of a number from an old article.

Exemptions and credits that lower a bill

Delaware offers a school tax credit for seniors, a county exemption for low-income seniors and the disabled, and full exemptions for government, school, religious and some charitable property. Most require an application, and most have a spring deadline.

  • Senior School Property Tax Credit: the owner must be 65 or older and the property must be the primary residence. Applications are due April 30. Residency rules depend on when you became a Delaware domiciliary: before 2013, no waiting period beyond eligibility in the following tax year; from 2013 through 2017, three consecutive years; from January 1, 2018, ten consecutive years. The bill must be paid in full by the end of the tax year. Confirm the current cap with your county before relying on a figure.
  • Kent County senior and disability exemption: age 65 by May 31 or total disability, income limits of $18,000 for one applicant or $24,750 combined with a spouse, and yearly reapplication by April 30. Title must be in the applicant's name.
  • General exemptions: government property, school property used for education, religious property not held as an investment, certain charitable property and parkland owned by civic groups such as homeowners' associations.

Sussex County sends applications for its senior, disability and State 65 exemptions through the Billing Office at (302) 855-7871.

How to appeal your assessment

Appeal in writing to your county, and treat the deadlines as firm. In Kent County an annual appeal must reach the Assessment Office by 5:00 p.m. on January 31 to affect the tax year beginning June 1, and a postmark does not count. Appeals of quarterly supplemental increases must be filed within 30 days of notice. Deadlines can shift in reassessment years. For New Castle County, the Board of Assessment Review deadline is March 15.

During a reassessment there is also an informal review with the contractor, Tyler Technologies, before the formal county appeal.

Look at refund rules before you sell. Kent County's refund policy follows state law and covers limited cases, such as tax paid while an appeal is pending or a duplicate bill. An error found after the appeal window usually does not produce a refund, because Delaware law puts the burden of making sure assessment data is accurate on the property owner.

An appeal still open at closing is a loose end. Tell the title company about it so the proceeds and any refund are handled in writing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Delaware houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a Delaware house with property tax due

Unpaid property tax is collected out of the sale or, if it stays unpaid long enough, through a court-supervised tax sale. Expect the title company to find the balance and pay it from proceeds at closing.

Under the monition method in the Delaware Code, the tax collector files in Superior Court, the sheriff posts a notice on the property, and the notice gives 20 days to pay before the tax authority can ask for a sale. After a tax sale the owner has 60 days after court approval to redeem by paying the purchaser the price plus 15 percent and costs. Kent County's sheriff procedures describe tax sales about every three months, with the full bid due the same day.

If you owe, work through this list.

  • Pull the current bill and any supplemental bills from the county tax portal.
  • Check whether a mortgage escrow already paid it. Sussex County offers an EscrowCheck tool and forwards bills to mortgage companies.
  • After closing, report the ownership change to the county assessment office. Sussex lists (302) 855-7824 for ownership changes.
  • Keep proof of payment for any exemption you are leaving behind.

A cash buyer who takes the house as-is can close with the tax balance paid from proceeds, often the simplest route when back taxes are growing by the month. Any figure depends on the county records for your parcel.

Frequently asked questions

Does Delaware have a state property tax?

Property tax is billed by counties and school districts. Your bill comes from the county tax office and reflects your school district's rate.

When is the Delaware property tax due date?

Kent and Sussex counties list September 30 for the annual bill. New Castle County's code sets July 1 with penalties after September 1, so check the due date printed on your New Castle bill.

Will selling my house trigger a new assessment?

Not in Kent County, where a sale does not trigger reassessment. Values change only for a countywide reassessment, a change to the property or a corrected error. Delaware counties now reassess every five years.

Can seniors reduce Delaware property tax?

Yes. The state Senior School Property Tax Credit covers homeowners 65 and older on their primary residence, with an April 30 application deadline. Kent County also has an income-limited senior and disability exemption.

Can I sell a Delaware house to a cash buyer if I owe back taxes?

Yes, in many cases. The tax balance is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company confirms the payoff with the county. The earlier you sell, the less penalty builds up.

title: Delaware Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling
content:
Delaware Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Delaware?

Does Delaware have an estate tax or inheritance tax today?

No. Delaware has neither tax for people who die after December 31, 2017. The estate tax was repealed for individuals dying after that date by 81 Del. Laws c. 52 (HB 16).

The inheritance tax went first. Chapter 13 of Title 30 of the Delaware Code, the inheritance tax chapter, now carries the label "Repealed." A 1998 law ended the inheritance tax effective January 1, 1999 and reshaped the estate tax so it applied only to estates large enough to need a federal estate tax return.

For heirs planning to sell a Delaware house, that is good news about one cost and no news about the others. The state does not tax the inheritance itself, but a sale can still trigger realty transfer tax and county property tax, and possibly federal rules.

How the estate tax worked before repeal

For deaths before January 1, 2018, Delaware taxed the value of an estate at death, using the federal estate tax as its starting point. This matters if the person who owned your house died in 2017 or earlier.

A resident's Delaware taxable estate was the modified federal taxable estate, reduced but not below zero by the federal applicable exclusion amount. For 2017 that exclusion was $5,490,000 for an individual. Rates were graduated, with a top rate capped at 16%.

DateChange
July 1, 1998 (effective January 1, 1999)Inheritance tax repealed; estate tax revised to follow the federal return requirement
July 1, 2009Estate tax effectively reinstated with a four-year sunset
March 28, 2013Sunset eliminated
July 2, 2017 (effective January 1, 2018)Estate tax repealed for individuals dying after December 31, 2017

An owner who died before 2018 and an estate still open

The old rules may still matter. Check with the Register of Wills or an estate attorney. The repealed sections of Chapter 15 of Title 30 carry notes pointing to 81 Del. Laws c. 52, section 2 on how the repeal applies. The old filing rules were these.

  • Both the return and the payment were due nine months after death.
  • The Division of Revenue could extend filing and payment time on written request. If the federal return was extended, the Delaware return was extended for a like period.
  • Late tax drew interest of one-half of one percent a month, and a failure-to-pay penalty of 1% a month could add up to 25%.
  • For nonresidents, a special lien attached to Delaware real and tangible property until the tax was paid.

The Sussex County Register of Wills publishes form NDETRR99, an affidavit that no Delaware estate tax return is required, for decedents who died from January 1, 1999 through December 31, 2017. The personal representative or a surviving joint tenant signs it before a notary, lists any Delaware real property, and cites 30 Del. C. 1505. An older estate that never cleared title may need that paper before a buyer will close.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Delaware house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Federal estate tax and a Delaware house

Only very large estates owe federal estate tax. For calendar year 2026 the basic exclusion is $15,000,000, a rise from $13,990,000 in 2025. A surviving spouse may take over the decedent's unused exclusion by electing on a timely estate tax return, as has been possible since January 1, 2011.

One house rarely comes close. If the estate holds many assets, or you are unsure, ask a CPA or estate attorney. The answer decides whether a federal return is needed at all, so get it before the house is listed rather than after an offer is in hand.

Realty transfer tax when an inherited house changes hands

Sometimes it applies. Delaware's realty transfer tax is separate from the estate tax, and some family transfers are excluded. The rules are in Chapter 54 of Title 30.

Section 5401(1) says a taxable "document" does not include a will or a transfer on death deed. It also leaves out conveyances between spouses, between parent and child or the child's spouse, between siblings, half siblings or step siblings, and between grandparent and grandchild or the grandchild's spouse.

Selling to an outside buyer changes things. Section 5402 sets 3% of value, dropping to 2.5% where the county or municipality has already enacted its full 1.5% share. In total the state and local tax comes to 4%: 2.5% for the state and 1.5% for the county or municipality. Grantor and grantee divide it equally, though section 5412 puts the duty to pay on the grantor unless they agree differently. Estates and trusts are listed among grantor categories without a special exemption, so if a personal representative signs the deed, confirm the treatment with the county Recorder of Deeds.

Selling an inherited Delaware house, step by step

The process runs through probate, title and the county. New Castle, Kent and Sussex counties each run a separate Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds. Which office you use follows the county where the house stands.

  1. Open the estate with the Register of Wills in the county and have the personal representative appointed.
  2. Resolve any open estate tax paperwork if the death was before 2018.
  3. Pay or settle county and school property taxes. Under Title 9, taxes in New Castle and Sussex are due July 1 and in Kent June 1.
  4. Sign a deed and pay realty transfer tax at recording, with proof of payment on the document. Section 5408 bars recording a deed that lacks it.
  5. Hand over the house as the contract requires. In a cash sale that can mean as-is.

Late county taxes cost money. In New Castle County the collecting authority adds a 6% penalty after September 1 plus 1% a month on the unpaid balance. In Kent and Sussex, a penalty of 1.5% per month starts after September 30 of the year the tax duplicate is delivered.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Delaware houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Delaware housing context for heirs

Delaware is mostly owner-occupied. Roughly 73.0% of housing units are owner-occupied, and the statewide median value for those homes is $352,000. That is a statewide number and no appraisal of your house.

Heirs who would rather not keep the house can sell it to a cash buyer who closes as-is, which spares repairs and clean-out on a property in a distant county. Terms vary by house, and an attorney should review the estate side. A cash sale also skips showings and a buyer's loan approval, so it fits an estate that wants to close out. Gather the death certificate, the letters from the Register of Wills, the deed, and the latest county tax bill before you talk to a buyer. Those four papers answer most of what a buyer and title company ask first.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a Delaware inheritance tax?

No. Chapter 13 of Title 30, the inheritance tax chapter, is marked repealed, and the repeal took effect January 1, 1999.

When was the Delaware estate tax repealed?

It was repealed for individuals dying after December 31, 2017. The repeal was approved July 2, 2017 as 81 Del. Laws c. 52 (HB 16).

What is the federal estate tax exclusion for 2026?

For 2026 the figure is $15,000,000, up from $13,990,000 in 2025.

Do I pay realty transfer tax if I inherit a Delaware house?

Not for a will or a transfer on death deed. Under 30 Del. C. 5401, transfers between parent and child, siblings, or grandparent and grandchild are excluded too. An outside sale carries 4% in total, shared equally by buyer and seller unless the contract differs.

Where do I record the deed for an inherited Delaware house?

Take it to the county Recorder of Deeds where the house sits. Proof of realty transfer tax payment, or an affidavit explaining why none is owed, must accompany the document.

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Delaware Sheriff Sales sale
  • Turn the Delaware Sheriff Sales offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Delaware House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Delaware?
We buy Delaware houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

How a Delaware sheriff sale works

A sheriff sale is a public auction of real estate run by the county sheriff to satisfy a court judgment, usually a mortgage foreclosure or unpaid taxes. The highest bidder wins, and the Superior Court then confirms the sale before any deed is delivered.

Delaware has three counties, and each sheriff runs sales a little differently. You'll run into mortgage foreclosure sales, tax sales (also called monition sales) and, in some counties, goods and chattels sales involving personal property.

  • Foreclosure sales: the plaintiff's attorney gives the opening bid, then bidders raise it out loud.
  • Tax or monition sales: the county or town sells a property for unpaid taxes or fees, and the owner may redeem afterward.
  • Confirmation: the court reviews the sale before the sheriff signs a deed.

For an owner facing a sale date, the real questions are how much time is left and what can be done before the auction.

Sale dates, places and payment deadlines

Kent County holds mortgage foreclosure sales usually on the first Thursday of the month. Sussex County holds them on the third Tuesday of each month at 9:30 a.m. Sales happen at government buildings, never at the property.

Sale detailKent CountySussex County
Foreclosure sale dayUsually the first Thursday of the month, unless a holidayThird Tuesday of each month, 9:30 a.m.
LocationLevy Court Chambers, 555 Bay Rd., DoverSheriff's Office conference room, 2nd floor, 22215 N. Dupont Blvd., Georgetown
Registration8:30 to 9:30 a.m.9:00 to 9:30 a.m.
Bidder deposit$4,000 per property$4,000 to register
Mortgage sale down payment20% of bid20% of bid
Tax sale paymentFull bid by 2:00 p.m. on sale dayFull bid by 3 p.m. on sale day

Kent County advertises its sales in the Dover Post and the Delaware State News two weeks ahead, and its tax sales come around about every three months.

Notice an owner must receive

The sheriff has to advertise the sale, and the plaintiff has to send notice to interested parties. Under 10 Del. C. section 4973, notice of a real estate sale goes up at least 10 days before the sale in 10 public places in the county, including the hundred where the property lies and each adjoining hundred, and runs for two weeks in two newspapers.

Superior Court Civil Rule 69(g) adds a mailing duty. At least seven days before the sale, the plaintiff or its counsel sends notice by certified mail, return receipt requested, to lienholders, tenants, record owners and other holders of recorded interests. The notice is also posted on a common entrance or area of the building. No sheriff's sale goes forward until proof of mailing and posting has been filed.

A July 2026 Superior Court order shows why notice matters. In New Castle County v. Coleman, the court set aside a June 9, 2026 sale of a Newark property and denied confirmation because the first mortgage holder never got actual notice that a stay had been lifted. The sale price was roughly half of that holder's security interest.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Delaware house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Payment and default rules for the winning bidder

The winner pays a deposit on sale day and the balance about a month later. A bidder who fails to pay forfeits the deposit, and the property is sold again.

  • Deposit: $4,000 in Kent County, by cashier's check, certified check or money order payable to the sheriff, applied toward the 20 percent down payment.
  • Foreclosure down payment: Kent wants the rest of the 20 percent by 2:00 p.m. on sale day, with the 80 percent balance due about 30 days later on the third Monday of the following month. Sussex wants 20 percent by 3 p.m. and the balance on the third Monday of the following month.
  • Forfeiture: in Kent, a buyer who misses the 2:00 p.m. payment loses the deposit and may be barred from future sales. In Sussex, failing to pay the balance forfeits the sale and the non-refundable 20 percent.
  • As-is: Sussex properties sell as-is and sight unseen, bidders may not trespass, and the winner is responsible for any liens.

Neither county guarantees clear title. Both tell bidders to search the Recorder of Deeds and the Prothonotary's Office first.

The sale is taxed too. Under 30 Del. C. section 5404, realty transfer tax is paid first out of the proceeds of a judicial sale, except where the buyer files an affidavit that the transfer to a defaulted lender is exempt.

Court confirmation and the deed

Under Superior Court Civil Rule 69(d), the sheriff's return is due on the third Monday of the month after the sale. Objections must be filed by the first Thursday after the return date. With no objection, the sale is confirmed automatically the following Friday.

Sussex County describes the same rhythm: sales are confirmed on the first Friday after the third Monday of the following month. In Kent County, the buyer's attorney prepares the deed after confirmation and the sheriff signs it.

After confirmation, 10 Del. C. section 4976 requires the sheriff to deliver a good and sufficient deed. Section 4985 discharges the real estate from liens against the defendant, except prior mortgages, to the extent the sale proceeds apply. Under section 4978, the purchaser is entitled to rent from the day of sale.

Ownership changes only when a proper deed is recorded. Our guide to recording a Delaware deed covers the fees and affidavits.

Money left over after the sale

Sometimes, yes. If a sale brings in more than the debt, the court may hold the excess. Delaware's Superior Court runs Project Rightful Owner, a page listing former owners, sold property addresses, court-held amounts, sale dates and case numbers for New Castle, Kent and Sussex counties.

Under 10 Del. C. section 4986, proceeds that can't be paid because the entitled persons are absent, unknown or incompetent go to the court that issued the process. Paying into court discharges the selling officer from liability for that money.

The Project Rightful Owner pages point claimants to petition requirements and attorney listings. If you lost a house at a sheriff sale in the past, search the list by surname.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Delaware houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to do before your house goes to sale

You can sell the house before the sale date, and a sale before the auction lets you keep any equity. Kent County's procedures give tax sales a redemption period of about 90 days, with the buyer getting the bid back plus 15 percent if the owner redeems. Foreclosure sales carry no redemption period.

In Sussex County, monition property can't be possessed until 60 days after confirmation, and sheriff sale property comes with no automatic eviction of occupants. An auction buyer has to plan for that.

Steps worth taking:

  • Get the exact sale date and case number from the sheriff and the Prothonotary.
  • Ask the plaintiff's attorney for a payoff figure.
  • Weigh whether a buyer who closes quickly beats the auction result.
  • Ask about loss-mitigation and mediation steps, which apply to owner-occupied homes.

A cash buyer can often close faster than an auction timeline allows, but the sale still has to pay off the liens of record. Cash Home Buyers can't promise a price and will go over the numbers with you.

Frequently asked questions

What is a sheriff sale in Delaware?

It's a public auction of real estate run by the county sheriff under a court order, usually after a mortgage foreclosure or for unpaid taxes. The Superior Court must confirm the sale before a deed is delivered.

Is there a redemption period after a Delaware foreclosure sale?

Kent County says foreclosure sales have none. Tax sales do: the owner has 60 days after the court approves the sale to redeem by paying the buyer the price plus 15 percent and costs.

How much do I need to bid at a Delaware sheriff sale?

Kent and Sussex counties both require a $4,000 deposit to bid. On a foreclosure the winner then pays 20 percent of the bid in total on sale day and the balance by the third Monday of the following month.

Do sheriff sale buyers get the keys right away?

No. Occupants aren't automatically evicted in Sussex County, and buyers may not enter before confirmation. Ownership changes when a proper deed is recorded.

Can a sheriff sale be stopped or postponed?

In Sussex County a sale can be stayed until 9:30 a.m. on sale day. Courts can also set a sale aside for irregularities, as in New Castle County v. Coleman in 2026, so watch for notice of any change.

Where to record a deed in Delaware

A deed gets recorded with the Recorder of Deeds in the county where the land sits: New Castle, Kent or Sussex. Title 25 of the Delaware Code gives a deed recorded in one county effect only for land in that county.

The three offices are separate, and each sets its own fees. Delaware law has the New Castle and Sussex recorders' fees set by ordinance, and Kent's work the same way.

  • New Castle County: 800 N. French St., 4th Floor, Wilmington, DE 19801. Phone (302) 395-7700.
  • Kent County: the Deeds Office at the county administrative complex, 555 Bay Rd., Dover. Phone (302) 744-2300, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Sussex County: 2 The Circle, Georgetown, DE 19947. Open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday, with the recording window closing at 4:00 p.m.

New Castle's office is the repository for land transaction records, corporate filings and financing statements in the county. Sussex's job is to record and index documents correctly and collect the right fees and taxes.

What the recorder requires on a deed

A deed has to meet a short list of statutory requirements before the recorder will take it. They come from 9 Del. C. section 9605 and 30 Del. C. chapter 54.

  • Affidavit of residence and gain: required with any deed conveying title to real estate, unless the transfer is one of the exempt transactions in the transfer tax law.
  • Preparer's name: the deed must carry the words "prepared by" followed by the name and address of whoever drafted it.
  • Value: the deed states the true, full and complete value, or comes with an affidavit giving the value and the reason, if any, the deed is not taxable.
  • Proof of tax: a taxable document is not recorded without proof the realty transfer tax was paid.
  • Correct fees: Kent County won't record a deed until the right fees and taxes are collected, and a $20 rejection fee may apply.

Some deeds need extra wording. When a lot in an unincorporated suburban community fronts a private road the State doesn't maintain, the deed has to say so before it can be recorded.

Treat the list as a checklist when you prepare a deed for a quick sale. A missing preparer line or affidavit gets the deed bounced, and the closing slips with it.

Recording fees by county

Recording fees are small next to the transfer tax, and they differ by county. Kent County's schedule took effect June 1, 2024. New Castle County raised its fees on September 28, 2026.

FeeKent CountyNew Castle County
Document fee$36.00 (includes $30 State, $1 County, $5 Technology)$30.00 state document fee per document
Page fee$10.00 per page, including the first pageRaised from $13.00 to $15.00 per page
Technology feeIncluded in document feeRaised from $5.00 to $7.00
Deed extra$5.00 per tax parcel (map number)Ask the office
Non-conforming document$40.00Ask the office
Rejection$20.00Ask the office

Two statutory charges ride on every recorded document. Under 9 Del. C. section 9607, the recorder collects a $5 Housing Development Fund surcharge and a $25 Delaware Cultural Access Fund fee, both folded into the county's assessment fee.

For Sussex County's current fees, call (302) 855-7785 before you send a check.

Realty transfer tax and who pays it

The realty transfer tax is 3 percent of the property's value, or 2.5 percent where the county or municipality has enacted the full 1.5 percent local tax. The statute splits it equally between grantor and grantee, and section 5412 puts the burden on the grantor unless the parties agree otherwise. In a sale contract, that makes the tax a point to settle in writing.

"Value" means the actual consideration, including liens and encumbrances. If the price falls below the highest appraised value for local tax purposes, value becomes that appraised figure unless a party shows fair market value is lower. Proof of an arm's length sale between unrelated parties is enough to show fair market value.

A few rules matter most to sellers:

  • No tax applies if the value is under $100.
  • A first-time home buyer's share drops by one half of one percent of the lesser of the value or $400,000. Only the grantee's portion shrinks, so the seller's share stays put.
  • Payment is shown by documentary stamp or another method the Department of Finance allows, and the recorder acts as stamp agent.
  • On a judicial sale, the tax comes out of the proceeds first, ahead of other claims and costs.

Avoiding the tax carries penalties. Presenting a document without the full tax paid is unlawful, with a fine up to $500 and up to one year in prison.

Municipal rates can stack on the county's. Kent County's recorder posts a rate form covering state, county and municipal taxes, and tax questions go to the Division of Revenue Tax Conferee at (302) 577-8651.

Which Delaware deeds are exempt from transfer tax?

Section 5401 of Title 30 lists more than two dozen kinds of conveyance that aren't taxed as documents. These come up often in home sales and family transfers:

  • Wills and transfer on death deeds, and mortgages.
  • Conveyances between spouses, and between former spouses after the divorce decree for property acquired during the marriage.
  • Conveyances between parent and child, between siblings, and between grandparent and grandchild.
  • A conveyance to a lender holding a bona fide mortgage that is genuinely in default, through a sheriff's foreclosure sale or a deed in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Conveyances to or from the United States, Delaware, their agencies and political subdivisions, and certain nonprofits.
  • Conveyances to a land bank.

Exempt still means recorded. The deed or an accompanying affidavit has to give the value and the reason the document is exempt. When a lender buys at foreclosure, the grantee signs the affidavit.

Say you inherit a Delaware house and want to deed it to a sibling. The sibling exemption can apply, but have a tax professional or attorney confirm it before closing.

Electronic recording

It's allowed where the county recorder has chosen to accept electronic documents. The electronic recording subchapter of Title 25 lets a recorder receive, index and store them under standards set by the Electronic Recording Commission, made up of each county's recorder and two members appointed by the Secretary of State.

A recorder who accepts electronic filings must keep accepting paper and must index both in the same index. Fees and taxes may be collected electronically. An electronic signature satisfies a signature requirement, and a notary's electronic signature plus the other required information satisfies notarization.

Sussex County's recorder runs a recording activity notification service and its deed records are searchable online. Kent County links an online deed search from its Deeds Office page. Each office decides what it will take, so ask before you plan on e-recording.

Nonresident sellers

A seller who lives out of state may have estimated income tax collected at the recorder's counter. Under 9 Del. C. section 9607(e), before recording a deed from a nonresident individual, pass-through entity or corporation, the recorder collects the required tax return and any estimated income tax reported due.

The recorder passes that money to the Secretary of Finance by the 20th of the month after recording. It's the seller's state income tax on the gain, separate from the transfer tax.

Owners outside Delaware, common with inherited and rental property, should raise this return with the closing agent early. A missing return holds up the deed.

Frequently asked questions

How long does recording a deed take in Delaware?

Ask the office or your title company for current timing. Sussex County closes its recording window at 4:00 p.m. each business day, and the recorder notes the date of reception once the instrument arrives.

What is the Delaware realty transfer tax rate?

It's 3 percent of value, or 2.5 percent where the county or municipality has enacted the full 1.5 percent local tax. Buyer and seller share it equally unless the contract says otherwise.

Who pays the transfer tax in Delaware, the buyer or the seller?

The statute splits it equally between grantor and grantee. Between the two, the grantor bears the burden unless they agree differently, so the sales contract controls.

Is there a first-time home buyer break on Delaware transfer tax?

Yes. The buyer's share is reduced by one half of one percent of the lesser of the value or $400,000. It applies to the buyer's portion only.

Can I record a deed without paying the fees up front?

No. The recorder may require payment once the date of reception is noted, and Kent County won't record a deed until the correct fees and taxes are collected.
